newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil firm on stronger crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil firm on stronger crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up late afternoon on Monday as the market firmed in response to stronger crude values and firmer open for gas oil futures in London, brokers said.
"The market firmed because of ACCESS (WTI crude) and the IPE (International Petroleum Exchange) gas oil," one broker said.
Front-month January gas oil swaps were last quoted at $30.40/$30.60 per barrel, from midday's $30.20/$30.40, brokers said.

Traders said the fundamentals remained bearish as demand from China, especially for February cargoes, have slowed down considerably as the market winds down for the Lunar New year which begins on February 7.
Usually the Chinese market is closed for about 10-days for the holidays, they said.
Fuel oil was steady as the market came to terms with the increased availabilties which have led to a big drop in prices last week.
Front-month January was last quoted at $115.75/$116.75 per tonne, from Friday's $116.25/$117.00, brokers said.
On Friday, in the physical market, a major offered 20,000-tonne loading in February 3-7 at $118.00 per tonne, down $3 a tonne from Thursday's offer price.
